solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Form of transport that might contain eight kings and queen

parts.note: a single pack of cards holds four kings, so two packs together, a double deck, would hold eight
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A riddle about a vehicle big enough to carry eight kings and a queen in royal procession.
explanation.walkthrough: The kings are playing cards, not monarchs: four to a pack, so eight need two packs. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the standard crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-storey bus, familiar on British streets, is a means of transport.

clue.text: Clubs in dead heat struggling halfway through Olympic city's event

indicators.note: in says the clubs letter sits inside the dead-plus-heat piece

parts.note: d. is the abbreviation for dead, as in family trees

indicators.note: struggling says the letters of heat are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: halfway through says the city's name is cut off after its first half

parts.note: London hosted the Olympic Games, most recently in 2012

explanation.surface: Clubs fight it out in a tied race at an Olympic host city's athletics event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges HEAT to EATH, and 'in' puts C inside D + EATH; 'halfway through' cuts LONDON to LON. 'dead heat' looks like a tied race, but it splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-part athletics contest is one of the sporting competitions held at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Extremist sect rejecting Catholic god

indicators.note: rejecting says the Catholic letter is thrown out of the sect word

parts.note: a cult is a sect or religious group
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A fanatical sect turns its back on the Catholic god.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding extreme views is called an ultra, as in ultra-right or ultra-loyalist.

clue.text: Pale one's outwardly glowing

indicators.note: outwardly says the glowing word lies on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: something glowing is lit up
one's read as one is gives I'M

explanation.surface: Someone pale who is nevertheless shining on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' is a noun here, a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale', not the adjective for wan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a fence or boundary, so it marks a bound or extent.

clue.text: Killer quadruped taking control of southern city in ancient times

indicators.note: taking control of says the animal word takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: a deer is a four-footed animal
Troy was the ancient city besieged by the Greeks

explanation.surface: A deadly four-legged creature seizes a southern city in antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wrecks or kills is a destroyer; the word is also a warship, a killer of other ships.

clue.text: Provide sound barrier for hideous noise

parts.note: to cater is to provide food or what is needed

indicators.note: sound says the barrier word is to be taken as it is said, not as spelt

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: An instruction to build soundproofing against a horrible din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound barrier' looks like the supersonic phrase, but 'sound' signals that WAUL is said like WALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's yowling at night is the classic shrill, ugly racket.

clue.text: Speak highly of former charge for the most part

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: for the most part says the charge word loses its last letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge, as on a bridge or road

explanation.surface: Praising an old fee, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, a synonym of speaking highly of.

clue.text: Suited, scruffy person put tie on to go out

indicators.note: to go out says the tied word goes around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: corded means tied up with cord

indicators.note: scruffy says the letters of person are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A scruffy man smartens up with a tie before heading out for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' is the anagram signal; 'put tie on' is the tied-with-cord word, which 'to go out' wraps around the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that match or agree are said to correspond, so suited and matched mean the same.

clue.text: Note I put on page in book (it's one I mentioned before)

indicators.note: in says the page group sits inside the book letters

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is the crossword book

indicators.note: put on says the note and I follow the page letter

parts.note: C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A footnote placed on a page of a book, referring to a work cited earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation, opere citato, sends a reader back to a work already quoted earlier in the text.

clue.text: Master said test's wrong, inaccurately expressed

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are put together in an incorrect order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster claimed the exam was mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misstated has been put incorrectly, which is to say expressed with errors.

clue.text: Shifting mountains I had seen rising, to fuse together

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says these pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: the Alps are a European mountain range
I had contracts to I'd
to cement is to bind or join firmly

explanation.surface: Mountains seen rising, then fused together, as in shifting continents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ALPS + ID into DISPLA; 'seen' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Displacement is the act of moving something from its place, a synonym of shifting.

clue.text: Retired player, after run, pulling muscle

indicators.note: after says the player comes behind the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an actor is a stage player

explanation.surface: A sportsman who retired after a run because he pulled a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling muscle' looks like an injury; it is the definition, a muscle that pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor muscle draws a body part back in, so it is a muscle that pulls.

clue.text: Islands in France, to the east of river in Angers

indicators.note: to the east of, in an across clue, says the islands come to the right of the river letter

parts.note: îles is French for islands

explanation.surface: French islands lying east of a river in the city of Angers.
explanation.walkthrough: Angers is a French city on the surface, but the definition is the verb: annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to irritate or annoy them, so it angers them.

clue.text: Seafood in market — get last of coley, not bothering about the rest?

indicators.note: in says the seafood goes inside the market word

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them
fish is food from the sea

indicators.note: last of says only the final letter of coley is taken

explanation.surface: Buying seafood at the market, taking the last of the coley and not caring about other shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: Coley is a cheap white fish common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without regard for other people is behaving in a self-centred way.

clue.text: Spontaneous spirit put out about rule by order

indicators.note: about says the spirit and scrambled put go around the remaining pieces

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous spirit

indicators.note: out says the letters of put are knocked out of order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A spirit expelled on a whim, by rule and by order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT to PTU; 'about' puts IMP and PTU either side of R + OM. The Order of Merit (OM) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu remark is made without preparation, on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: A pub with a quiz ending with difficult round (random)

indicators.note: round says the difficult word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: hard means difficult
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: ending says only the last letter of quiz is used

explanation.surface: A pub quiz finishing with a tough round, whose questions are random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a quiz round, but it is the container signal; 'ending' takes Z from quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard lacks any plan or order, a synonym of random.

clue.text: A Northern European recoiling in dismay

indicators.note: recoiling says the European word springs backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in far northern Europe

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian shrinks back in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: King Edward, perhaps non-smoker, but consuming one, or more than one drink

indicators.note: consuming says the other pieces swallow the letter for one

parts.note: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato
one is the Roman numeral I
NS is the abbreviation for non-smoker

explanation.surface: A king, who perhaps does not smoke, but does drink.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a potato variety, not the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is an alcoholic drink or a drinking bout; the plural means several drinks.

clue.text: Have wrong to confess

parts.note: to own something is to have it
something up is wrong, as in what's up?

explanation.surface: Having done wrong, one must confess.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom for admitting a misdeed.

clue.text: Comeback for urban Los Angeles music wrecked

indicators.note: comeback says the whole series of pieces is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: urban describes the city
rap is a style of music

explanation.surface: A revival for urban music from Los Angeles goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' is slang for very drunk, not ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British slang for helplessly drunk.

clue.text: Degree's the thing to do

parts.note: it means the thing, as in that's it

explanation.surface: A degree is the essential thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is the abbreviation do., meaning the same again in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The ditto mark, abbreviated do., means the same as above.

clue.text: Keep time or we'll intervene

indicators.note: intervene says the pronoun comes between the letters of or

parts.note: we'll, we will, gives the pronoun we

explanation.surface: A warning to keep time, or others will step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is a noun, a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep of a castle is its central fortified stronghold, a tall stone structure.

clue.text: Way to solve problem of capped right molar decaying

indicators.note: decaying says the letters crumble and re-form in a new order
capped says the head is taken off the word right

explanation.surface: A crowned back tooth on the right side rotting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capped' sounds dental but removes R from RIGHT; IGHT + MOLAR is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-by-step procedure for working out a calculation or task is exactly that.

clue.text: Zest of bergamot… sugar… coming up

indicators.note: coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Citrus zest from bergamot, with sugar, as in a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enthusiasm or relish, which is zest in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Damage half of cerebellum with old instrument

indicators.note: damage says the letters are knocked about into a new order
half of says only the first five of the ten letters are used

explanation.surface: Injury to half the brain caused by an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval bowed stringed instrument, a forerunner of the violin.

clue.text: Doesn't make much of blue stage shows

parts.note: blue means sad or down
plays are dramas performed on stage

explanation.surface: Someone dismissive of depressing or risqué theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to minimise it, giving it little weight.

clue.text: Exhausted former PM changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides says the right letter is swapped for the left letter

parts.note: Gordon Brown was British prime minister 2007-2010

explanation.surface: A worn-out ex-prime minister who has defected to the other party.
explanation.definitionFit: Blown describes being out of breath, as a winded horse is, so tired out.

clue.text: Is stuffing added to mashed up soldiers?

indicators.note: added to says the stuffing word comes after the mashed word

parts.note: ground means crushed or mashed up
forces means is stuffing, as forcemeat is stuffing

explanation.surface: A cooking question: is stuffing mixed into the mash?
explanation.definitionFit: Land-based military troops, as against air or naval forces, are an army's men.
